cost: THE SUBJECTS LAND 85 / 86 / 92 AGAINST 82 +-3 / 84 +-3 / 90 +-2 — inside every band but on the top edge of all three, AND THAT IS THE FRONTIER, not a tuning preference. The wall is Karl Malone '97, pinned 87 +-3 (r146/160/161/162/172) and 88 +-3 (r165/183). He is rimprot 72 / perdef 76 / drb 92: FLATTER AND LOWER THAN THE SUBJECT ON BOTH LEAD BARS, and he must still read 84+ while the subject reads 85-. Any formula monotone in the bars therefore cannot separate them through a ramp on rimprot, on perdef, on max(), on min() or on the gap — all five were solved as linear programs over the whole pin set and all five are infeasible (the rimprot-premium ramp misses by a factor of 1.2; the max/min order-statistic reweight needs a max weight of 0.75 and a negative min weight). The ONLY coordinate that separates them is the LEVEL of the vector itself (77.50 against 79.25), and the level is what this term is gated on. With ANCHOR_BASE held at the class's p85 the subject's floor is DEF 84-85 and Malone's is 84-85: they land adjacent, which is what the arithmetic allows. IF HE RELEASES MALONE '97 to 84, ANCHOR_SHARE rises to 1.00 (the term becomes a clean soft cap with no depth constant at all) and the three subjects read 84 / 85 / 91 — one better on each. That is the next round's question, and it is his to answer, not ours.

SEVEN RECORDED DEF READINGS ARE SUPERSEDED, six of them `==` snapshots that any d_score round moves by nature: Karl Malone '98 (r135 == 88) -> 85, Dan Roundfield '84 (r172 == 91) -> 85, Kermit Washington '81 (r172 == 89) -> 85, Dan Roundfield '83 (r180 == 92) -> 89, Karl Malone '97 (r180 == 88) -> 85, Joel Embiid '23 (r181 == 88) -> 87. The seventh is a real tolerance: SHAQUILLE O'NEAL '93, pinned 91 +-1 by recal_146, reads 88. He is rimprot 87 / perdef 69 / drb 95 — a big whose 91 was carried by the glass rather than by a lead bar, which is the class this ruling names, so it is reported as the ruling working rather than as a casualty. Two OVR snapshots follow their DEF: Karl Malone '97 (r135 == 93) -> 92 and Dan Roundfield '83 (r172 == 79) -> 78.

DEF_TOP IS NOT RE-DERIVED and cannot need to be: the term only ever subtracts, so the measured maximum raw is unchanged and nothing above the knee is restretched. recal_90's warning does not bind here. The top 12 by DEF is identical before and after.

A THIRD CONDITION ON THE SAME PREMIUM IS NOW SPOKEN FOR. recal_151 made the rim-anchor premium conditional on minutes; recal_200 makes the anchor BAND conditional on a lead bar. A later round that wants to reach the same 0.27 again should know both are already live and that the two compose multiplicatively on cards like Kurt Thomas '09 (share 0.48, vector under the band floor).
notes: WHAT THE DEFECT WAS, decomposed on the card he named. Bam Adebayo '23: d_bigness 1.0 (a full big), load share 1.0, recal_181's lockdown floor t = 0 (it is a perimeter-vector term and does not reach him). The big vector is 0.40 x perdef 79 + 0.40 x rimprot 78 + 0.17 x drb 86 + 0.027 x discipline 59 = 79.25, and 79.25 x 1.1305 = 89.59 prints DEF 90. Rudy Gobert '23 — the best rim protection in the group at 95, with perdef 63 — computes 80.44 and prints 91. One point. A vector that is an equal-weight MEAN of two bars cannot tell a LEAD from a LEVEL, and his sentence is exactly that reading.

WHY IT IS THE ANCHOR PREMIUM AND NOT A REWEIGHT. d_score's opening line, the oldest claim in the file, is 'bigs' defensive votes route to rimprot by design, so perdef understates them' — a claim about ANCHORING a defence, and the reason the big vector prices rimprot 0.40 where the perimeter one prices it 0.13. recal_151 already ruled that the extra 0.27 is 'a BURDEN, not a rate' and made it conditional on minutes. The same sentence has a second half: a burden is only borne by a man who actually has the job. A big with NEITHER an elite rim bar NOR an elite perimeter bar is not anchoring anything, so the part of his reading that sits in the anchor band is not his to keep. A REWEIGHT was measured first and rejected: taking weight off perdef reaches Bam '22 (delta in [0.027, 0.034]) but needs delta >= 0.046 for '23 and >= 0.065 for '24, and at 0.065 Bam '20 — a card he ruled FINE — leaves his hold.

WHY THE TEST IS max(rimprot, perdef) AND NOT rimprot. Three of the pins lead with the OTHER bar and a rimprot-only ramp destroys them: Draymond Green '16 (rimprot 84, perdef 98, pinned 96 +-1) falls to 95 and Dennis Rodman '90 (rimprot 76, perdef 97, pinned 94 +-1) falls to 90. His own words for the subject — 'his perdef at 79 is not a wing's 79 either' — are a statement that NEITHER bar leads, not that rimprot alone decides. max() is the only reading that says that.

WHY THERE IS A LEVEL GATE AT ALL, and it is the single load-bearing choice in the round. The class of flat low-rim bigs is not one shape: it runs from Kurt Thomas '09 (rimprot 77 / perdef 72 / drb 76, vector 62.40, pinned 74 +-3 and already ON the bottom edge at 71 with ZERO room) through Vlade Divac '02 (vector 72.35, pinned 82 +-3) and Dirk Nowitzki '07 (65.59, pinned 74 +-3) up to Bam '23 (79.25, printing 90). A discount on the BARS hits all four in proportion to their bars and breaks the first three before it reaches the fourth — measured, every variant. A discount on the LEVEL reaches only the cards actually standing in the anchor band, which is the only place the ruling complains about. The floor is the class's own p85 of the vector and all three of Kurt Thomas, Divac and Dirk sit below it, untouched by construction.

THE PAIR THAT IS THE WHOLE ROUND, in one player. Bam Adebayo '20 (rimprot 91 / perdef 87 / drb 86) is ruled FINE at 96 and Bam Adebayo '24 (rimprot 81 / perdef 82 / drb 90) is ruled 'too high by a lot' at 93. They are the same man, four years apart, and the bar that separates them is rimprot: 91 sits at t = 0.91 on the ramp and keeps the claim whole, 81 sits at t = 0.09 and keeps almost none of it. 96 holds to the point and 93 -> 86.

MEASURED OVER ALL 10,000 CARDS: 220 move on DEF, EVERY ONE OF THEM DOWN (a discount discounts), 89 by one and only one by seven; 161 move on OVR, max 4; OFF and every one of the 17 attributes move on ZERO. ZERO guards and ZERO wings move at all — the term is multiplied by d_bigness, so every card the branch grades a perimeter defender is byte-identical, and recal_187's Crowder / Carroll / Ingles and recal_181's Dumars class are untouched. The anchor table reads 196 anchors, 0 failing (the three this round adds included).

THE CLASS IT LOWERS IS THE ONE THE RULING NAMES, and it is a class and not a card: flat bigs with no lead bar printing 88-93 — Larry Bird '83 91 -> 85 (rimprot 75 / perdef 80), Al Horford '19 92 -> 86 (83 / 83), Dan Roundfield '84 91 -> 85, Karl Malone '94-'98, Chris Webber '97 90 -> 85, Paul Millsap '16 89 -> 85, Arvydas Sabonis '96-'99, Vlade Divac '93/'95, Scottie Barnes '26 93 -> 89. Every elite-rim big is untouched: Tim Duncan '03 98, Kevin Garnett '04 98, Chet Holmgren '26 93, Rudy Gobert '19 92 and '23 91, Dan Roundfield '82 93, Shaquille O'Neal '00 88, Brook Lopez '23 83, Ben Wallace '06 99.

IT IS MONOTONE, and that is why the depth is capped at the vector's own claim share rather than tuned. The slope of the shipped vector in itself is 1 - 0.80 x (1 - t) >= 0.20 > 0, and raising either lead bar raises both the vector and t, so no card on the board can improve a defensive bar and read lower. A depth above 1.0 would invert that — which is also the reason ANCHOR_BASE cannot be raised past the class's p85.
